title: Separate request authorization from control-plane recovery
description: Choose a condition. Active routes show authentication, policy, secret issuance, audit durability, storage quorum, seal dependencies, and restore paths.

nodes.label: Workload client
nodes.detail: Authenticates, requests only the required path, renews when allowed, reloads rotated material, and handles denial or unavailability.

nodes.label: Auth method
nodes.detail: Validates workload or human evidence and maps it to token policies, TTL limits, aliases, and metadata.

nodes.label: Vault active node
nodes.detail: Evaluates capabilities, routes the request, records leases, and coordinates revocation through one active control-plane leader.

nodes.label: Database secrets engine
nodes.detail: Uses a configured administrative connection to create, rotate, and revoke unique database credentials from approved roles.

nodes.label: Application database
nodes.detail: Accepts the generated credential until the database expires, disables, or deletes it. Vault availability is not the same as database revocation success.

nodes.label: Audit device A
nodes.detail: Receives request and response audit records. Vault must successfully write to at least one enabled audit device to service an audited request.

nodes.label: Audit device B
nodes.detail: Provides another write target and must be monitored and analyzed with other device logs for a complete record.

nodes.label: Integrated Raft storage
nodes.detail: Stores encrypted Vault state under consensus. Quorum loss stops writes; snapshots provide a separate recovery input.

nodes.label: Seal mechanism
nodes.detail: Protects the key material needed to decrypt Vault's barrier. Auto-unseal creates a lifecycle dependency on this external mechanism.

nodes.label: Protected snapshot
nodes.detail: Captures integrated-storage state for recovery. Restoring it still requires compatible seal access, cluster bootstrap, validation, and client cutover.

scenarios.label: Issue a dynamic secret
scenarios.summary: The client authenticates, policy permits one database role, Vault creates an external credential, writes audit records, stores the lease, and returns the credential with its lease.
scenarios.result: The credential is unique and leased. The client must renew or replace it, while Vault must retain enough authority and connectivity to revoke it later.

scenarios.label: Revoke the token tree
scenarios.summary: An operator or identity lifecycle event revokes the client token. Vault walks child leases and asks each secrets engine to invalidate its external credentials.
scenarios.result: New Vault requests are denied immediately. External credential invalidation still depends on the plugin and target system; monitor revocation failures and retry queues.

scenarios.label: One audit device fails
scenarios.summary: The local audit sink cannot accept the record, but the independent remote device still writes successfully.
scenarios.result: The request can proceed because at least one enabled device succeeded. Alert immediately and combine device logs carefully because neither device alone is guaranteed complete.

scenarios.label: All audit devices fail
scenarios.summary: No enabled audit device can persist the request and response record.
scenarios.result: Vault refuses the audited request. Audit storage capacity, rotation, connectivity, and recovery are availability dependencies, not optional reporting.

scenarios.label: Auto-unseal dependency lost
scenarios.summary: A restarted node has encrypted Raft state but cannot reach or use the configured KMS or HSM key.
scenarios.result: The node remains sealed. Recovery keys do not decrypt the root key when the auto-unseal mechanism is permanently lost; protect and rehearse the external seal lifecycle.

scenarios.label: Restore from a snapshot
scenarios.summary: Operators bootstrap a controlled recovery path, provide compatible seal access, restore an integrated-storage snapshot, validate state, and redirect clients.
scenarios.result: A successful file restore is not completion. Verify cluster health, auth mounts, policies, leases, audit devices, secret-engine connectivity, and client re-authentication before cutover.
